Detect and split range values

Source: R/numeric_parser.R
split_ranges.Rd

Determines whether a normalized remainder string represents a numeric range (e.g., "5-10", "-10–5", "-10-5") rather than a negative number or scientific notation. Returns split low/mid/high values for ranges.

Usage

split_ranges(remainder, qualifier)

Arguments

remainder

Character vector (post-qualifier-extraction, post-normalization)

qualifier

Character vector (matching length, from extract_qualifier)

Value

A list with logical is_range, numeric low, mid, high (NA for non-ranges)

Details

Pre-guard order (per D-04): (a) If qualifier is non-empty, it is NOT a range (qualified values are single rows) (b) Apply range regex that captures optional leading negative, full decimal/exponent numbers, then a hyphen separator, then a second full number (c) Negative sign immediately after 'e'/'E' is part of exponent, not a range separator
